Definition: from G2896; an outcry (in notification, tumult or grief):--clamour, cry(-ing).
BiblicalUsage: Krauge is the outcry itself, the noise of a crowd or the sound of grief. It rises in Acts 23:9 when the Pharisees raise a great cry for Paul, it is the "clamour" Paul tells believers to put away in Ephesians 4:31, it is the "strong crying and tears" of Christ in Hebrews 5:7, and it is the cry at midnight in Matthew 25:6, "Behold, the bridegroom cometh."
TheologicalSignificance: What I take from it is that the word draws a line between two kinds of crying: the clamour we are told to put away, and the cry of prayer that God hears, and I want mine to be the second. I want my cry to be prayer, not clamour, and God knows the difference.
